title: Unified description of random motions and generalized Fokker-Planck equations
abstract: This review surveys diverse types of random motion within a unified framework, introducing essential mathematical tools, including special functions and fractional calculus, in a pedagogical manner. We focus on generalized random motions in one-dimensional space described by Fokker-Planck like equations, whose fundamental solutions take a universal and simple form in the Laplace-Fourier domain in terms of a generic function $\varphi(s)$. By exploring the functional forms of $\varphi(s)$ consistent with physical constraints, we derive a broad class of stochastic dynamics. This includes Brownian and active motion, simple and anomalous diffusion, and processes featuring stochastic resetting or trapping mechanisms. For each case, we provide the corresponding kinetic equation, explicit solutions (where available), and mean-square displacements alongside their asymptotic behaviors. Finally, we discuss the physical interpretation of these motions through the lens of time-changed processes and subordinators.
summary: This review unifies the description of various random motions, from simple diffusion to anomalous transport, using a generalized Fokker-Planck equation approach. By analyzing the fundamental solution in the Laplace-Fourier domain via a function $\varphi(s)$, the authors derive a broad class of stochastic dynamics. This provides a powerful mathematical tool for characterizing non-Markovian processes in condensed matter and statistical physics.
main_problem: To provide a unified mathematical framework for describing diverse types of random motions in one dimension, particularly those governed by generalized Fokker-Planck-like equations.
main_result: The framework successfully unifies descriptions for simple diffusion, anomalous diffusion, active motion, and processes with stochastic resetting by relating them to the functional form of a generic function $\varphi(s)$ in the Laplace-Fourier domain.
method: The analysis uses Laplace and Fourier transforms to solve the generalized integro-differential equation, identifying constraints on the function $\varphi(s)$ using concepts from Bernstein functions and fractional calculus.
model_or_system: The model is a generic one-dimensional random motion characterized by a single-time Probability Density Function $P(x, t)$, which is governed by a generalized Fokker-Planck equation. Specific physical examples include Brownian motion, active transport, and processes with trapping.
key_observables: The Probability Density Function $P(x, t)$, the Mean-Square Displacement (MSD) $\langle x^2(t) angle$, and the long-time power-law exponent $\mu$ of the MSD.

main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on drift-free stochastic processes in the absence of external potentials, and the mathematical simplification relies on the fundamental solution having a Lorentzian shape in the Fourier-Laplace domain.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the general theory using the Laplace-Fourier domain, deriving the universal solution form involving $\varphi(s)$, and then systematically applying this framework to derive and analyze specific stochastic dynamics, including interpretations via time-changed processes and subordinators.
why_interesting: The mathematical tools developed (Bernstein functions, fractional calculus) are central to modeling non-Markovian dynamics, which are crucial for describing complex open quantum systems or transport phenomena in mesoscopic physics.
